name: binding request
why: The 20-byte request from the post: type 0x0001, no attributes. It asks for the address and says nothing else, so there is nothing to check, nothing to fix and no attribute table.

fields.label: Message
fields.note: 0x0001. It asks the server which address it sees, and carries nothing else.

fields.label: Integrity
fields.note: No FINGERPRINT or MESSAGE-INTEGRITY.

name: binding answer
why: The post's answer: XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS f523 e112a648 un-XORs to 192.0.2.10:54321, the port XOR 0x2112 and the address XOR 0x2112A442, worked by hand.

expect.caption: 1 attribute, each padded to 4 bytes
rows: IPv4. The port is 0xF523 XOR 0x2112 and the address 0xE112A648 XOR 0x2112A442.

name: binding answer header
why: 0x0101 is method 1 with class 2: the class bits sit at positions 4 and 8, between the method's, which is why a success is 0x0101 and not 0x0102.

fields.label: Message type
fields.note: Method 0x001, Binding, and class 2, success response, with their bits interleaved.

fields.label: Length
fields.note: Of attributes, after the 20-byte header.

fields.label: Magic cookie
fields.note: Always the same. It tells STUN apart from the media sharing the port.

fields.label: Transaction ID
fields.note: Random, so the answer can be matched to the request.

name: ice connectivity check
why: Made by aioice: USERNAME srv7:alce, receiver first, USE-CANDIDATE, and MESSAGE-INTEGRITY and FINGERPRINT that both verify with the server's password.

fields.label: Message
fields.note: 0x0001. An ICE connectivity check from "alce" to "srv7" that nominates this pair.

name: its answer
why: The success response to that check, made by aioice: the mapped address, and both integrity checks verify with the same password, since an ICE answer is signed with the request's key.

fields.label: Mapped address
fields.note: Where the server saw the sender.

name: turn 401
why: A TURN server's 401 to an Allocate without credentials. The remedy is RFC 8656's: retry with USERNAME, the REALM and NONCE from this response, and MESSAGE-INTEGRITY. FINGERPRINT verifies, so nothing else is listed.

expect.caption: What to fix, most serious first
rows: Send the request again with USERNAME, and the REALM and NONCE from this response, signed with MESSAGE-INTEGRITY keyed with MD5 of username:realm:password.

name: a wrong magic cookie is not STUN
why: The cookie is fixed; anything else is another protocol or the original STUN of RFC 3489, and is refused rather than guessed at. No later offset has a cookie either, so nothing is skipped.

expect.message: The magic cookie is 0x2112A443, but STUN's is always 0x2112A442. This is probably not a STUN message, or it is the older RFC 3489 kind.

name: a length the message does not have
why: The header promises 8 bytes of attributes and none follow.

expect.message: The header says 8 bytes of attributes follow, but only 0 do.

name: a corrupted fingerprint is caught
why: The demo's request with FINGERPRINT, last bit flipped: the CRC no longer matches, and the answer's integrity line says so, in red, the only tone in it.

name: not hex
why: Stray characters are named rather than filtered out.

expect.message: This is not hex: it contains "h", "l", "o", "t", "r". Expected hex digits, optionally separated by spaces, colons or commas.

name: rfc 5769 sample request
why: RFC 5769 section 2.1, an independent vector: an ICE check from h6vY to evtj whose HMAC-SHA1 and CRC-32 the RFC publishes.

fields.label: Message
fields.note: 0x0001. An ICE connectivity check from "h6vY" to "evtj".

name: rfc 5769 ipv4 response
why: RFC 5769 section 2.2: the RFC says the mapped address is 192.0.2.1 port 32853, and both checks verify with the same password.

fields.label: Mapped address
fields.note: Where the server saw the sender.

name: rfc 5769 ipv6 response
why: RFC 5769 section 2.3: the RFC says 2001:db8:1234:5678:11:2233:4455:6677 port 32853, un-XORed with the cookie and the transaction ID.

fields.label: Mapped address
fields.note: Where the server saw the sender.

name: rfc 5769 long-term credentials, before SASLprep
why: RFC 5769 section 2.4: the key is MD5 of username:realm:password, and the password as the RFC gives it, The<U+00AD>M<U+00AA>tr<U+2168>, only matches after SASLprep makes it TheMatrIX.

expect.caption: 4 attributes, each padded to 4 bytes
rows: A value the server chose, to be sent back with the next request.
The server's name for the set of accounts the password belongs to.
It matches. The key is MD5 of "マトリックス:example.org:password", a long-term credential as TURN uses, after SASLprep turned the password into "TheMatrIX".

name: a wrong long-term password
why: One letter's case wrong: the HMAC fails, and the fix names all three parts of the key.

expect.caption: What to fix, most serious first
rows: MESSAGE-INTEGRITY: the key tried is MD5 of "マトリックス:example.org:password", a long-term credential as TURN uses.
Check the TURN password, and the username and realm. All three go into the key.

name: a frame copied from wireshark
why: Wireshark's Copy as Hex Dump of a whole frame: the offsets and the ASCII column are dropped, and the 42 bytes of Ethernet, IPv4 and UDP headers are recognised and skipped.

name: a figure pasted from an rfc
why: RFC 5769's own figure, notes and braces included: the notes after a wide gap are ignored, and the message is the 2.1 request.
